To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

when HeLa cells are fused together by the use of Sendai virus, the multinucleate cells which form from these fusions exhibit a high degree of co-ordination of DNA synthesis and of mitosis, and that this co-ordination can be maintained in multinucleate cells for several days.
when two HeLa cells are fused, the resultant multinucleated cells undergo synchronous DNA synthesis and mitotic cycles.
when two or more HeLa cells fuse together, the nuclei of the resulting multinucleate cells rapidly co-ordinate their DNA synthesis and mitotic activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of cell growth and the control of the cell cycle, and with the role of the cell nucleus in these processes.
the study of the mechanisms involved in the co-ordination of nuclear events within the multinucleate cells which are formed by the fusion of animal cells in culture.
the regulation of DNA synthesis and cell division, and with the mechanisms which control the cell cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ability of a cell to co- ordinate nuclear events is not affected by the presence of a virus.

the multinucleate cells resulting from cell fusion can co-ordinate nuclear activities in a way similar to that of a single cell, and that this co-ordination occurs rapidly and without any apparent impairment of the ability to maintain synchrony.
the ability of fused cells to co-ordinate the nuclear events of the cell cycle is not impaired by virus-mediated cell fusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multinucleate cells behave in a manner which is consistent with the hypothesis that the nucleus contains a clock which controls cell division.
the multinucleate cells which we have studied are able to impose synchrony upon themselves by mechanisms which are not dependent upon the use of the virus to effect the fusion of the cells.
the multinucleate HeLa cell is a useful model for the study of the mechanisms involved in the co-ordination of DNA replication and mitosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cell cycle of a single nucleus in a multinucleate cell is not significantly different from that of the nucleus of a single HeLa cell growing in culture.
cell fusion is a very powerful method to synchronize cells in culture.
the cell cycle can be synchronized by cell fusion.
